sanskrit: vipatākaṃ viyantāraṃ vivarmadhvajajīvitam taṃ kṛtvā dviradaṃ bhūyaḥ sahadevo 'ṅgam abhyagāt
english: Having stripped that elephant of its banner, its driver, its armour, its standard, and its very life, Sahadeva once more bore down upon the king of Aṅga.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ tu nakulo vārayitvāṅgam ārdayat nārācair yamadaṇḍābhais tribhir nāgaṃ śatena ca
english: But Nakula, holding Sahadeva back, himself afflicted the Aṅga, striking the king with three iron shafts like the rods of Yama, and the elephant with a hundred.

sanskrit: divākarakaraprakhyān aṅgaś cikṣepa tomarān nakulāya śatāny aṣṭau tridhaikaikaṃ tu so 'cchinat
english: The Aṅga hurled at Nakula eight hundred javelins bright as the rays of the sun, but he cut each one into three pieces.

sanskrit: tathārdhacandreṇa śiras tasya ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ sa papāta hato mlecchas tenaiva saha dantinā
english: Then with a crescent-headed arrow the Pāṇḍava severed his head, and the slain barbarian fell to the ground together with his tusked beast.

sanskrit: ācāryaputre nihate hastiśikṣāviśārade aṅgāḥ kruddhā mahāmātrā nāgair nakulam abhyayuḥ
english: When the preceptor's son, skilled in the lore of elephants, had been slain, the enraged elephant-drivers of the Aṅgas rushed upon Nakula with their beasts.

sanskrit: calatpatākaiḥ pramukhair hemakakṣyātanucchadaiḥ mimardiśantas tvaritāḥ pradīptair iva parvataiḥ
english: With fluttering banners on their foreheads, with golden girths and body-coverings, they came on swiftly, eager to crush him, like blazing mountains in motion.

sanskrit: mekalotkalakāliṅgā niṣādās tāmraliptakāḥ śaratomaravarṣāṇi vimuñcanto jighāṃsavaḥ
english: The Mekalas, Utkalas, and Kaliṅgas, the Niṣādas and the men of Tāmraliptaka, bent on slaughter, loosed showers of arrows and javelins.

sanskrit: taiś chādyamānaṃ nakulaṃ divākaram ivāmbudaiḥ pari petuḥ susaṃrabdhāḥ pāṇḍupāñcālasomakāḥ
english: Seeing Nakula overspread by them as the sun is veiled by clouds, the Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas, and Somakas, much enraged, rushed forward all around him.

sanskrit: tatas tad abhavad yuddhaṃ rathināṃ hastibhiḥ saha sṛjatāṃ śaravarṣāṇi tomarāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Then there arose a battle between the car-warriors and the elephants, both pouring forth showers of arrows and javelins by the thousand.

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ prasphuṭuḥ kumbhā marmāṇi vividhāni ca dantāś caivātividdhānāṃ nārācair bhūṣaṇāni ca
english: The frontal globes of the elephants burst asunder, and their various vital parts, and the tusks of the deeply pierced beasts, and their ornaments, were shattered by the iron shafts.

sanskrit: teṣām aṣṭau mahānāgāṃś catuḥṣaṣṭyā sutejanaiḥ sahadevo jaghānāśu te petuḥ saha sādibhiḥ
english: With sixty-four keenly sharpened arrows Sahadeva quickly slew eight of those great elephants, and they fell together with their riders.

sanskrit: añjogatibhir āyamya prayatnād dhanur uttamam nārācair ahanan nāgān nakulaḥ kuranandana
english: Drawing his excellent bow with effort, Nakula, O delight of the Kurus, smote the elephants with straight-flying iron shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaineyapāñcālyau draupadeyāḥ prabhadrakāḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahānāgān siṣicuḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then the descendant of Śini and the Pāñcāla prince, the sons of Draupadī, the Prabhadrakas, and Śikhaṇḍin drenched the great elephants with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: te pāṇḍuyodhāmbudharaiḥ śatrudviradaparvatāḥ bāṇavarṣair hatāḥ petur vajravarṣair ivācalāḥ
english: Those mountainlike elephants of the foe, struck by the arrow-showers of the Pāṇḍava warriors who were like rain-clouds, fell as mountains fall beneath downpours of thunderbolts.

sanskrit: evaṃ hatvā tava gajāṃs te pāṇḍunarakuñjarāḥ drutaṃ senām avaikṣanta bhinnakūlām ivāpagām
english: Having thus slain your elephants, those bulls among men of the Pāṇḍava side looked upon your army, swiftly scattering like a river whose banks have been breached.

sanskrit: te tāṃ senām avālokya pāṇḍuputrasya sainikāḥ vikṣobhayitvā ca punaḥ karṇam evābhidudruvuḥ
english: Beholding that host, the warriors of the son of Pāṇḍu threw it into confusion, and then once again rushed straight at Karṇa.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ tataḥ kruddhaṃ dahantaṃ tava vāhinīm duḥśāsano mahārāja bhrātā bhrātaram abhyayāt
english: Then, O great king, Duḥśāsana the brother advanced against his brother Sahadeva, who in his fury was consuming your host.

sanskrit: tau sametau mahāyuddhe dṛṣṭvā tatra narādhipāḥ siṃhanādaravāṃś cakrur vāsāṃsy ādudhuvuś ca ha
english: Seeing those two meet in mighty combat, the lords of men there raised lionlike roars and waved their garments aloft.

sanskrit: tato bhārata kruddhena tava putreṇa dhanvinā pāṇḍuputras tribhir bāṇair vakṣasy abhihato balī
english: Then, O Bhārata, the mighty son of Pāṇḍu was struck upon the chest with three arrows by your wrathful bowman son.

sanskrit: sahadevas tato rājan nārācena tavātmajam viddhvā vivyādha saptatyā sārathiṃ ca tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Thereupon, O king, Sahadeva pierced your son with an iron shaft, then struck him with seventy more and his charioteer with three apiece.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tadā rājaṃś chittvā cāpaṃ mahāhave sahadevaṃ trisaptatyā bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: Then, O king, Duḥśāsana, having cut his bow asunder in that great fray, afflicted Sahadeva with seventy-three shafts upon his arms and chest.

sanskrit: sahadevas tataḥ kruddhaḥ khaḍgaṃ gṛhya mahāhave vyāvidhyata yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śrīmāṃs tava sutaṃ prati
english: Then the wrathful Sahadeva, best of warriors and full of splendour, seized a sword in that great battle and whirled it at your son.

sanskrit: samārgaṇagaṇaṃ cāpaṃ chittvā tasya mahān asiḥ nipapāta tato bhūmau cyutaḥ sarpa ivāmbarāt
english: That great blade, having cut through his bow together with its fitted arrows, then fell to the earth like a serpent dropping from the sky.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sahadevaḥ pratāpavān duḥśāsanāya cikṣepa bāṇam antakaraṃ tataḥ
english: Then the valiant Sahadeva took up another bow and let fly at Duḥśāsana a death-dealing arrow.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ viśikhaṃ yamadaṇḍopamatviṣam khaḍgena śitadhāreṇa dvidhā ciccheda kauravaḥ
english: As that shaft came flying on, gleaming like the rod of Yama, the Kaurava cut it in two with his keen-edged sword.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā nistriṃśaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ pātayām āsa samare sahadevo hasann iva
english: As that sword came suddenly hurtling on, Sahadeva, as if smiling, struck it down in the battle with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tato bāṇāṃś catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ tava putro mahāraṇe sahadevarathe tūrṇaṃ pātayām āsa bhārata
english: Then, O Bhārata, your son in that great battle quickly let fall sixty-four arrows upon Sahadeva's car.

sanskrit: tāñ śarān samare rājan vegenāpatato bahūn ekaikaṃ pañcabhir bāṇaiḥ sahadevo nyakṛntata
english: Those many arrows speeding upon him in the fight, O king, Sahadeva cut to pieces, each one with five shafts.

sanskrit: sa nivārya mahābāṇāṃs tava putreṇa preṣitān athāsmai subahūn bāṇān mādrīputraḥ samācinot
english: Having warded off the great arrows sent by your son, the son of Mādrī then gathered very many shafts and aimed them at him.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja sahadevaḥ pratāpavān samādhatta śaraṃ ghoraṃ mṛtyukālāntakopamam vikṛṣya balavac cāpaṃ tava putrāya so 'sṛjat
english: Then in his fury, O great king, the valiant Sahadeva fitted a dreadful shaft like Death, Time, and the Ender, and drawing his bow mightily, loosed it at your son.

sanskrit: sa taṃ nirbhidya vegena bhittvā ca kavacaṃ mahat prāviśad dharaṇīṃ rājan valmīkam iva pannagaḥ tataḥ sa mumuhe rājaṃs tava putro mahārathaḥ
english: Piercing him with speed and rending his great armour, the shaft entered the earth, O king, as a serpent enters an anthill; and thereupon, O king, your son, that mighty car-warrior, swooned away.

sanskrit: mūḍhaṃ cainaṃ samālakṣya sārathis tvarito ratham apovāha bhṛśaṃ trasto vadhyamānaṃ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Seeing him senseless, his charioteer, sorely afraid, swiftly bore the car away as it was being raked by sharp arrows.

sanskrit: parājitya raṇe taṃ tu pāṇḍavaḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja duryodhanabalaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ prāmathad vai samantataḥ
english: Having vanquished him in battle, the son of Pāṇḍu, O descendant of Pāṇḍu's line, joyfully crushed Duryodhana's force on every side.

sanskrit: pipīlikāpuṭaṃ rājan yathāmṛdnān naro ruṣā tathā sā kauravī senā mṛditā tena bhārata
english: As a man in anger tramples an anthill of ants, O king, so was that Kaurava army crushed by him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe dārayantaṃ varūthinīm karṇo vaikartano rājan vārayām āsa vai tadā
english: Then, O king, Karṇa the son of the sun checked Nakula, who in his fury was rending the host asunder in the battle.

sanskrit: nakulaś ca tadā karṇaṃ prahasann idam abravīt cirasya bata dṛṣṭo 'haṃ daivataiḥ saumyacakṣuṣā
english: And Nakula, smiling, then said this to Karṇa: "After long, alas, the gods have looked upon me with kindly eyes,

sanskrit: yasya me tvaṃ raṇe pāpa cakṣurviṣayam āgataḥ tvaṃ hi mūlam anarthānāṃ vairasya kalahasya ca
english: since you, O wretch, have come within the range of my sight in battle. For you are the root of all our calamities, of the enmity and the strife.

sanskrit: tvaddoṣāt kuravaḥ kṣīṇāḥ samāsādya parasparam tvām adya samare hatvā kṛtakṛtyo 'smi vijvaraḥ
english: Through your fault the Kurus have been wasted, falling upon one another. Slaying you this day in battle, I shall have achieved my purpose and be freed of fever."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca nakulaṃ sūtanandanaḥ sadṛśaṃ rājaputrasya dhanvinaś ca viśeṣataḥ
english: Thus addressed, the son of the charioteer answered Nakula in words befitting a prince and, above all, a bowman:

sanskrit: praharasva raṇe bāla paśyāmas tava pauruṣam karma kṛtvā raṇe śūra tataḥ katthitum arhasi
english: "Strike in battle, O boy, that we may see your manhood. Having done some deed in the fight, O hero, then are you fit to boast.

sanskrit: anuktvā samare tāta śūrā yudhyanti śaktitaḥ sa yudhyasva mayā śaktyā vineṣye darpam adya te
english: Without speaking, my son, do the brave fight to the utmost of their power. So fight with me with all your might; this day I shall humble your pride."

sanskrit: ity uktvā prāharat tūrṇaṃ pāṇḍuputrāya sūtajaḥ vivyādha cainaṃ samare trisaptatyā śilīmukhaiḥ
english: Having said this, the charioteer's son swiftly smote the son of Pāṇḍu, and pierced him in the battle with seventy-three arrows.

sanskrit: nakulas tu tato viddhaḥ sūtaputreṇa bhārata aśītyāśīviṣaprakhyaiḥ sūtaputram avidhyata
english: Then Nakula, thus pierced by the charioteer's son, O Bhārata, struck the charioteer's son in turn with eighty shafts like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tasya karṇo dhanuś chittvā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ triṃśatā parameṣvāsaḥ śaraiḥ pāṇḍavam ārdayat
english: Karṇa, that foremost of archers, cut his bow asunder and afflicted the Pāṇḍava with thirty stone-whetted, golden-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā papuḥ śoṇitam āhave āśīviṣā yathā nāgā bhittvā gāṃ salilaṃ papuḥ
english: Piercing his armour, they drank his blood in the battle, as venomous serpents, having broken through the earth, drink water.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya hemapṛṣṭhaṃ durāsadam karṇaṃ vivyādha viṃśatyā sārathiṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, gold-backed and hard to withstand, he pierced Karṇa with twenty arrows and his charioteer with three.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja nakulaḥ paravīrahā kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena karṇasya dhanur acchinat
english: Then in his wrath, O great king, Nakula, slayer of hostile heroes, cut off Karṇa's bow with an exceedingly sharp razor-headed shaft.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ sāyakānāṃ śatais tribhiḥ ājaghne prahasan vīraḥ sarvalokamahāratham
english: Then, while his bow was severed, the hero, laughing, smote that mighty car-warrior renowned in all the worlds with three hundred shafts.

sanskrit: karṇam abhyarditaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍuputreṇa māriṣa vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmū rathinaḥ saha daivataiḥ
english: Seeing Karṇa thus sorely pressed by the son of Pāṇḍu, O sire, the car-warriors, together with the gods, were filled with the utmost amazement.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya karṇo vaikartanas tadā nakulaṃ pañcabhir bāṇair jatrudeśe samārdayat
english: Then Karṇa, the son of the sun, taking up another bow, afflicted Nakula with five arrows in the region of the collarbone.

sanskrit: uraḥsthair atha tair bāṇair mādrīputro vyarocata svaraśmibhir ivādityo bhuvane visṛjan prabhām
english: With those arrows fixed upon his breast, the son of Mādrī shone resplendent, like the sun shedding its light upon the world with its own rays.

sanskrit: nakulas tu tataḥ karṇaṃ viddhvā saptabhir āyasaiḥ athāsya dhanuṣaḥ koṭiṃ punaś ciccheda māriṣa
english: Then Nakula, having pierced Karṇa with seven iron shafts, once more cut off the tip of his bow, O sire.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya samare vegavattaram nakulasya tato bāṇaiḥ sarvato 'vārayad diśaḥ
english: Taking up another bow of swifter force in the battle, Karṇa then with his arrows blocked the quarters on every side around Nakula.

sanskrit: saṃchādyamānaḥ sahasā karṇacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ ciccheda sa śarāṃs tūrṇaṃ śarair eva mahārathaḥ
english: Being suddenly overspread by the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow, that great car-warrior swiftly cut those arrows asunder with arrows of his own.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ jālaṃ vitataṃ vyomny adṛśyata khadyotānāṃ gaṇair eva saṃpatadbhir yathā nabhaḥ
english: Then a net wrought of arrows was seen stretched across the sky, as the heavens appear when filled with swarms of darting fireflies.

sanskrit: tair vimuktaiḥ śaraśataiś chāditaṃ gaganaṃ tadā śalabhānāṃ yathā vrātais tadvad āsīt samākulam
english: By the hundreds of arrows loosed by the two, the sky was then covered over, and it was as thronged as when swarms of locusts fill it.

sanskrit: te śarā hemavikṛtāḥ saṃpatanto muhur muhuḥ śreṇīkṛtā abhāsanta haṃsāḥ śreṇīgatā iva
english: Those arrows wrought of gold, falling again and again in ordered rows, gleamed like ranks of wild geese flying in lines.

sanskrit: bāṇajālāvṛte vyomni chādite ca divākare samasarpat tato bhūtaṃ kiṃ cid eva viśāṃ pate
english: When the sky was veiled in the net of arrows and the sun was hidden, only with difficulty could any creature move about, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: niruddhe tatra mārge tu śarasaṃghaiḥ samantataḥ vyarocatāṃ mahābhāgau bālasūryāv ivoditau
english: With the path obstructed all around by masses of arrows, the two illustrious warriors shone like two newly risen morning suns.

sanskrit: karṇacāpacyutair bāṇair vadhyamānās tu somakāḥ avālīyanta rājendra vedanārtāḥ śarārditāḥ
english: The Somakas, being slain by the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow, shrank away, O king of kings, tormented by pain and afflicted by the shafts.

sanskrit: nakulasya tathā bāṇair vadhyamānā camūs tava vyaśīryata diśo rājan vātanunnā ivāmbudāḥ
english: Likewise your host, being slain by Nakula's arrows, scattered to the quarters, O king, as clouds are driven apart by the wind.

sanskrit: te sene vadhyamāne tu tābhyāṃ divyair mahāśaraiḥ śarapātam apakramya tataḥ prekṣakavat sthite
english: Both armies, being smitten by those two with great celestial arrows, withdrew beyond the reach of the shafts and then stood by as mere onlookers.

sanskrit: protsārite jane tasmin karṇapāṇḍavayoḥ śaraiḥ vivyādhāte mahātmānāv anyonyaṃ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: When the host had been driven back by the arrows of Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava, those two high-souled warriors pierced each other with showers of shafts.

sanskrit: nidarśayantau tv astrāṇi divyāni raṇamūrdhani chādayantau ca sahasā parasparavadhaiṣiṇau
english: Displaying their celestial weapons at the head of the battle and suddenly veiling each other, each sought the other's death.

sanskrit: nakulena śarā muktāḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavāsasaḥ te tu karṇam avacchādya vyatiṣṭhanta yathā pare
english: The arrows loosed by Nakula, feathered with heron and peacock plumes, having shrouded Karṇa, then took their stand as though foes encircling him.

sanskrit: śaraveśmapraviṣṭau tau dadṛśāte na kaiś cana candrasūryau yathā rājaṃś chādyamānau jalāgame
english: Entered as they were into a dwelling of arrows, neither could be seen by anyone, O king, like the moon and sun veiled at the coming of the rains.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe karṇaḥ kṛtvā ghorataraṃ vapuḥ pāṇḍavaṃ chādayām āsa samantāc charavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then Karṇa, wrathful in the fray, assuming a still more terrible aspect, covered the Pāṇḍava on every side with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: sa cchādyamānaḥ samare sūtaputreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ na cakāra vyathāṃ rājan bhāskaro jaladair yathā
english: Though overspread in the battle by the charioteer's son, the Pāṇḍava felt no distress, O king, like the sun amid the rain-clouds.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyādhirathiḥ śarajālāni māriṣa preṣayām āsa samare śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then the son of Adhiratha, laughing, O sire, sent forth nets of arrows in the battle by the hundred and by the thousand.

sanskrit: ekacchāyam abhūt sarvaṃ tasya bāṇair mahātmanaḥ abhracchāyeva saṃjajñe saṃpatadbhiḥ śarottamaiḥ
english: By the arrows of that great-souled one all became one unbroken shadow; with the excellent shafts falling thick, it grew like the shade of clouds.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja dhanuś chittvā mahātmanaḥ sārathiṃ pātayām āsa rathanīḍād dhasann iva
english: Then Karṇa, O great king, having cut the bow of that high-souled one, struck down his charioteer from the floor of the car, as if in sport.

sanskrit: tathāśvāṃś caturaś cāsya caturbhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ yamasya sadanaṃ tūrṇaṃ preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: And with four sharp arrows he swiftly dispatched his four horses to the abode of Yama, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athāsya taṃ rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ tilaśo vyadhamac charaiḥ patākāṃ cakrarakṣau ca dhvajaṃ khaḍgaṃ ca māriṣa śatacandraṃ tataś carma sarvopakaraṇāni ca
english: Then he swiftly shattered his car to fragments small as sesame seeds with his arrows, and his banner, his wheel-guards, his standard, his sword, O sire, his hundred-mooned shield, and all his equipment.

sanskrit: hatāśvo virathaś caiva vivarmā ca viśāṃ pate avatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ parighaṃ gṛhya viṣṭhitaḥ
english: His horses slain, his car destroyed, his armour gone, O lord of peoples, he quickly stepped down from the car and stood his ground, seizing an iron club.

sanskrit: tam udyataṃ mahāghoraṃ parighaṃ tasya sūtajaḥ vyahanat sāyakai rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: That uplifted, most terrible iron club of his the charioteer's son shattered with his shafts, O king, by the hundred and by the thousand.

sanskrit: vyāyudhaṃ cainam ālakṣya śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ ārdayad bahuśaḥ karṇo na cainaṃ samapīḍayat
english: Seeing him weaponless, Karṇa afflicted him many times over with smooth-jointed arrows, yet did not press him hard.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare kṛtāstreṇa balīyasā prādravat sahasā rājan nakulo vyākulendriyaḥ
english: Being smitten in the battle by that mightier master of arms, Nakula, his senses confounded, suddenly fled, O king.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya rādheyaḥ prahasan vai punaḥ punaḥ sajyam asya dhanuḥ kaṇṭhe so 'vāsṛjata bhārata
english: Rushing after him, the son of Rādhā, laughing again and again, cast his strung bow about Nakula's neck, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śuśubhe rājan kaṇṭhāsaktamahādhanuḥ pariveṣam anuprāpto yathā syād vyomni candramāḥ yathaiva ca sito meghaḥ śakracāpena śobhitaḥ
english: Then he shone resplendent, O king, with the great bow hung about his neck, as the moon in the sky encircled by a halo, or as a white cloud adorned by the bow of Indra.

sanskrit: tam abravīt tadā karṇo vyarthaṃ vyāhṛtavān asi vadedānīṃ punar hṛṣṭo vadhyaṃ māṃ tvaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then Karṇa said to him: "In vain have you spoken. Speak now again, full of joy, that I am one to be slain by you, again and again."
